CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: Deterministic offline/local benchmark runtime; no dependence on cloud credentials, privileged external infrastructure, internet services, or destructive host routing. Simulate or namespace route operations safely while preserving realistic Linux routing semantics and Ansible-managed multi-node behavior.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a production-style Go route control plane that models desired route and policy state, reconciles it across a multi-node Linux fleet, detects drift, protects management reachability, records revision history, and exposes the same lifecycle through an operator dashboard and Ansible-driven installation/configuration.

REQUIRED_END_STATE: At least 16 API operations spanning nodes, tables, routes, rules, revisions, preview/apply/rollback, drift/reconcile, rollouts, audit, health and dashboard summary.
All route mutations target an isolated deterministic kernel model.
Desired and observed state are revisioned and restart-recoverable.
Per-node failures are isolated during wave rollout with rollback.
Ansible installs binary/config/service and projects variables idempotently.
Frontend exposes inventory, route/rule state, revisions, drift and rollouts.

STATE_MODEL.persistence: Atomic JSON checkpoint with schema version, monotonic revision, desired/observed state, rollouts and audit; primary validation with last-known-good backup.
STATE_MODEL.concurrency: store compare-and-swap plus per-node serialization; immutable read snapshots
STATE_MODEL.safety: protected management CIDRs/interfaces/routes; unsafe plans rejected before publication

outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: Eight deterministic nodes across three sites, fourteen named route tables, IPv4/IPv6/multipath routes, policy rules, drift fixtures and revision history.
